title: Cold rebuild: What will git record?
summary: Rebuild What will git record? from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **What will git record?** in *Servers, sudo, diffs and git*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Why does `:w !sudo tee %` work when `:w` failed?
options: vim itself still runs as you; it only hands the text to `tee`, which runs as root via sudo and writes the file
steps.explain: `%` expands to the file name; the writing process is `tee`, not vim.

steps.title: Rebuild What will git record? cold
prompt: Write `string? CommitMessage(string[] lines)` modelling git's default cleanup of `COMMIT_EDITMSG`:
- remove trailing whitespace from each line,
- collapse runs of several blank lines into one, and drop blank lines at the start and end,
- if nothing is left, return `null` (git aborts: *Aborting commit due to empty commit message*).
Otherwise return the lines joined with `\n`.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
